witness: validator `epr:validator-interface-first-reuse` not registered — unresolvable reference routes to review rather than guessing. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory: the epr:validator-interface-first-reuse validator-EPR is not registered in v1, so this rule surfaces as an inject nudge — it never blocks.)

Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory: the epr:validator-interface-first-reuse validator-EPR is not registered in v1, so this rule surfaces as an inject nudge — it never blocks.)

subject: scripts/ci/verify-projected-head.sh
witness: validator `epr:validator-deploy-script-runtime` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. INVARIANT — deploy-container scripts are bash + coreutils ONLY. The render/deploy container has no python, no pip, no PyYAML — a script that imports one fails BEFORE `kubectl apply`, silently pinning the fleet on pre-fix builds (edge #1183 failed all 7 human deploys on a PyYAML import; it made the fixes it was gating look inert). Parse YAML/JSON with bash + coreutils (grep/sed/awk), not a python one-liner. And VERIFY where it RUNS, not just locally: a CI tool negative-tested outside its runtime is itself an unverified claim — the same class it polices. If a build-only script (e.g. cargo-publish-*.sh) legitimately needs a richer toolchain, confirm it never runs on the deploy path before proceeding.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 4029 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-heal-fills-never-moves` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. INVARIANT — heal FILLS absence or converges FORWARD; it never moves authority backwards. A projection-reconcile / stamp path uses `StampMode::{Declare, HealCanonical, GapFill}`: `Declare` is ONLY for deliberate canonical channels (declare route, propagation POST, own-conductor `ContentHeadDeclared` signal — request-borne/own-authored, may move a head anywhere including a deliberate revert); a heal with a canonical answer (`canonical == true`) MUST stamp `HealCanonical` — fill, same-head refresh, or a move ONLY with proof of forward ordering (`declared_at` newer than the stored `declared_head_at`; NULL either side = refuse): a conductor that has not yet integrated a newer canonical link answers with the OLD canonical record — canonical, yet stale — and an unconditional Declare stamp moved the head BACKWARDS (2026-07-12: elohim-host-landing converged at edge #1187's seam-smoke, healed back to the superseded head by #1188). A fallback resolve (`canonical == false`, e.g. a cold conductor's root-author election) MUST stamp `GapFill` — fill an empty row only (the 2026-07-11 resurrection class: HEALED anchor restamped the OLD head 2 min after cross-conductor adoption, across 2,838 divergence-queued rows). Do not widen `Declare`, and do not key the guard on *who* writes (that froze forward adoption, defect #3) — key it on the authority the write CARRIES (`canonical` + declaration ordering).

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
`projection_reconcile.rs` is 3592 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/eprfs/epr-cli/src/flow/fulfill.rs
witness:
validator `epr:validator-interface-first-reuse` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory: the epr:validator-interface-first-reuse validator-EPR is not registered in v1, so this rule surfaces as an inject nudge — it never blocks.)

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/metrics.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-heal-fills-never-moves` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. INVARIANT — heal FILLS absence or converges FORWARD; it never moves authority backwards. A projection-reconcile / stamp path uses `StampMode::{Declare, HealCanonical, GapFill}`: `Declare` is ONLY for deliberate canonical channels (declare route, propagation POST, own-conductor `ContentHeadDeclared` signal — request-borne/own-authored, may move a head anywhere including a deliberate revert); a heal with a canonical answer (`canonical == true`) MUST stamp `HealCanonical` — fill, same-head refresh, or a move ONLY with proof of forward ordering (`declared_at` newer than the stored `declared_head_at`; NULL either side = refuse): a conductor that has not yet integrated a newer canonical link answers with the OLD canonical record — canonical, yet stale — and an unconditional Declare stamp moved the head BACKWARDS (2026-07-12: elohim-host-landing converged at edge #1187's seam-smoke, healed back to the superseded head by #1188). A fallback resolve (`canonical == false`, e.g. a cold conductor's root-author election) MUST stamp `GapFill` — fill an empty row only (the 2026-07-11 resurrection class: HEALED anchor restamped the OLD head 2 min after cross-conductor adoption, across 2,838 divergence-queued rows). Do not widen `Declare`, and do not key the guard on *who* writes (that froze forward adoption, defect #3) — key it on the authority the write CARRIES (`canonical` + declaration ordering).

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness: `projection_reconcile.rs` is 3632 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

Do not widen `Declare`, and do not key the guard on *who* writes (that froze forward adoption, defect #3) — key it on the authority the write CARRIES (`canonical` + declaration ordering).

Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/metrics.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-heal-fills-never-moves` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. INVARIANT — heal FILLS absence or converges FORWARD; it never moves authority backwards. validator `epr:validator-interface-first-reuse` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory: the epr:validator-interface-first-reuse validator-EPR is not registered in v1, so this rule surfaces as an inject nudge — it never blocks.)

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/view_federation.rs
witness:
validator `epr:validator-interface-first-reuse` not registered — advisory only, not evaluated. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory: the epr:validator-interface-first-reuse validator-EPR is not registered in v1, so this rule surfaces as an inject nudge — it never blocks.)

witness: `projection_reconcile.rs` is 5454 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/signals.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

Static observation, no live metrics dependency — the value is reasoned once and held by the class.

`main.rs` is 4475 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: genesis/orchestrator/manifests/edgenode/alpha.yaml
witness: this concern already lives at scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh (the deterministic render/deploy gate that rejects the dead key by name). INVARIANT — `webrtc_config` passes VERBATIM into tx5's serde-camelCase `WebRtcConfig`. The ICE-server list key MUST be `iceServers` (camelCase). The snake_case `ice_servers` is an UNKNOWN field: serde silently drops it and the conductor runs with ZERO ICE servers — WebRTC survives on host candidates only while peers are co-located, then dies silently when topology spreads (adam→shem, 2026-05-27; 2,081 divergent anchors from the co-located era). Use `iceServers`, never `ice_servers`. The render gate `scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh` enforces this at deploy; do not ship a manifest it will reject. Evidence: Holochain conductor-config example (`iceServers`); tx5-connection `config.rs` `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.

The agency charter: agents self-grant `measure`/`inject` (+ `dispatch` with a named agent and prompt) freely — observation and advisory-with-directive cannot harm. `ask`/`deny` authorship or promotion is different in kind (it narrows or blocks another agent's future writes) and requires ratified authority from the DELIBERATING COMMUNITY — today the operator+agents working this tree (the "us" of the pre-p2p era), tomorrow a qahal — never agent self-declaration: narrow-never-widen applied to governance itself. Ratification is not a solo stamp; it is PEER ACCEPTANCE AT THE BRANCH RUNG: the branch ladder is the repo's reach axis (shift/* = self; dev = community; main = commons), a governance rule on a shift branch is structurally pending, and the dev-merge acceptance IS the ratification event — the CanonizationRef of repo governance (accepting a merge includes accepting the rules we govern ourselves by). This validator fires when a `.epr-meta` write INTRODUCES an ask|deny rule (a brand-new manifest: any ask|deny rule; an existing one: compared against its prior on-disk content, so unrelated edits to an already-governed manifest never retrigger) that is not backed by a `policy: <id>@<version>` binding whose registry row's `established_by` carries deliberation provenance (`deliberated-*`, or the legacy `operator-*` rows predating this convention). An INLINE ask|deny rule with no policy binding at all is never backed: the charter requires the deliberated registry pin for that class, not a rule authored directly in the manifest. `ask` tier: routes to review (refer_reason `escalation-requires-ratification`) rather than hard-blocking, since the gate cannot itself adjudicate ratification — only an operator can. Known v1 scope gap: `when` patterns match by BASENAME only (`_matches_when` in _lib/epr_meta.py), so this binding's `.epr-meta` scope covers the legacy flat manifest form but not the directory form (`.epr-meta/manifest.md`, basename `manifest.md`) — tighten if/when that form sees adoption. Bound at the repo root (not `.claude/epr-meta/.epr-meta`): `when` patterns are basename-only and the cascade is a strict ancestor walk, so a manifest placed anywhere other than the repo root can only ever govern writes BENEATH itself — it cannot reach out to unrelated directories. The sibling drift to sovereignty-ontology-guard, named by the operator on 2026-08-05: "ownership is like sovereignty — it might need a guard to help keep us from gravitating into it." OWNERSHIP is the enclosure-flavoured apex the protocol subordinates to STEWARDSHIP and CUSTODY. ValueFlows already splits the two — `primaryAccountable` (who holds the rights) vs `custodianScope` (who physically stewards), with distinct `transferCustody` and `transferAllRights` actions — and COLLAPSING them is exactly the enclosure failure the Georgist common-inheritance framing exists to prevent: a holon that "owns" the commons it stewards has enclosed it. The distinction is load-bearing for holonic land/commons stewardship, where the commons holds the rights and a local unit holds custody, and custody must be transferable without the rights ever moving. This guard fires on NET-NEW apex framing only (bare "own"/"owner" are far too common to gate — the phrase list is deliberately narrow and names only assertions that ownership is the RIGHT relationship to a resource). It is an AFFIRMATION prompt, not a ban. Confirm your usage is one of the LEGITIMATE frames and proceed, or reframe: (1) ADVERSARY — naming what is resisted (enclosure, platform data-ownership claims, rent extraction); (2) BOUNDED — ownership WITHIN a commons that retains the rights; (3) EXTERNAL-LEGIBILITY — describing an outside legal system's ownership on its own terms (a title, a co-op share, a jurisdiction's property register). Declare `stewardship-frame:` in the doc (a `sovereignty-frame:` marker also satisfies it — the two frames travel together) and the guard goes quiet. Parallel rule, same shape and same escape hatch: sovereignty-ontology-guard. subject: genesis/research/freenet-peer-confrontation-2026-07-27.md
witness: missing required frontmatter ['sovereignty-frame']. The MEMBRANE rule (operator decision 2026-08-05). Surveys must quote, reason inside, and argue against the prevailing self-sovereignty ontology, because nearly every project we survey still uses it (Playnet's "autonomic identifiers", p2panda/SSB's crypto-identity lineage, the whole DID/VC/UCAN stack). Prompting on every quotation would tax the critique itself and push authors toward euphemism — the opposite of clarity. So research does not gate the VOCABULARY; it gates the DIFFERENTIATION. A survey that reaches for the words declares `sovereignty-frame: adversary|bounded|bridge-legibility` in its frontmatter and says plainly how the Elohim ontology differs: identity is imago dei — an inviolable right BACKSTOPPED by community and institutional expression, never a self-asserted crypto primitive; real agency comes from the community backstopping the individual. Naming the frame is what quarantines it at the boundary, so an examined borrowing inoculates instead of leaking. The same marker is the ONLY silencer for the global PostToolUse landing-logger, so one line does both jobs. Birth-time only — maintenance of an existing survey is never trapped. The membrane ends at this directory: canon (genesis/docs/content/elohim-protocol/) binds the unrelaxed sovereignty-ontology-guard policy, where an apex frame would become doctrine rather than a quotation.

subject: scripts/ci/dead-config-lint.sh
witness: this concern already lives at each deploy script's own header requirement (bash + coreutils only), scarred by edge #1183. INVARIANT — deploy-container scripts are bash + coreutils ONLY. The render/deploy container has no python, no pip, no PyYAML — a script that imports one fails BEFORE `kubectl apply`, silently pinning the fleet on pre-fix builds (edge #1183 failed all 7 human deploys on a PyYAML import; it made the fixes it was gating look inert). Parse YAML/JSON with bash + coreutils (grep/sed/awk), not a python one-liner. And VERIFY where it RUNS, not just locally: a CI tool negative-tested outside its runtime is itself an unverified claim — the same class it polices. If a build-only script (e.g. cargo-publish-*.sh) legitimately needs a richer toolchain, confirm it never runs on the deploy path before proceeding.

subject: .claude/scripts/habits-status.py
witness: validator `epr:validator-brand-vocabulary-boundary` flagged this write. Product and architecture prose may use the protocol's domain brands; compilable artifacts should name the capability an unfamiliar engineer is actually working with. Prefer identity, learning, work, community or collective governance, economy or value flow, and the precise governance concept (judgment, decision, policy, commitment, authority, or recovery quorum) in symbols, routes, schemas, persistence names, and wire values. The validator is net-new-only and ignores documentation, comments, and schema prose, so existing debt can be cleaned incrementally without tolling unrelated maintenance. This repository is still pre-compatibility: internal package ids, Holochain roles and zomes, persisted discriminators, and wire literals do not earn an exception merely because we already use them. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

Surveys must quote, reason inside, and argue against the prevailing self-sovereignty ontology, because nearly every project we survey still uses it (Playnet's "autonomic identifiers", p2panda/SSB's crypto-identity lineage, the whole DID/VC/UCAN stack). Prompting on every quotation would tax the critique itself and push authors toward euphemism — the opposite of clarity. So research does not gate the VOCABULARY; it gates the DIFFERENTIATION. A survey that reaches for the words declares `sovereignty-frame: adversary|bounded|bridge-legibility` in its frontmatter and says plainly how the Elohim ontology differs: identity is imago dei — an inviolable right BACKSTOPPED by community and institutional expression, never a self-asserted crypto primitive; real agency comes from the community backstopping the individual. Naming the frame is what quarantines it at the boundary, so an examined borrowing inoculates instead of leaking. The same marker is the ONLY silencer for the global PostToolUse landing-logger, so one line does both jobs. Birth-time only — maintenance of an existing survey is never trapped. The membrane ends at this directory: canon (genesis/docs/content/elohim-protocol/) binds the unrelaxed sovereignty-ontology-guard policy, where an apex frame would become doctrine rather than a quotation.

subject: scripts/ci/dead-config-lint.sh
witness: this concern already lives at each deploy script's own header requirement (bash + coreutils only), scarred by edge #1183. INVARIANT — deploy-container scripts are bash + coreutils ONLY. The render/deploy container has no python, no pip, no PyYAML — a script that imports one fails BEFORE `kubectl apply`, silently pinning the fleet on pre-fix builds (edge #1183 failed all 7 human deploys on a PyYAML import; it made the fixes it was gating look inert). Parse YAML/JSON with bash + coreutils (grep/sed/awk), not a python one-liner. And VERIFY where it RUNS, not just locally: a CI tool negative-tested outside its runtime is itself an unverified claim — the same class it polices. If a build-only script (e.g. cargo-publish-*.sh) legitimately needs a richer toolchain, confirm it never runs on the deploy path before proceeding.

subject: /projects/elohim/genesis/orchestrator/manifests/edgenode/alpha.yaml
witness:
this concern already lives at scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh (the deterministic render/deploy gate that rejects the dead key by name). INVARIANT — `webrtc_config` passes VERBATIM into tx5's serde-camelCase `WebRtcConfig`. The ICE-server list key MUST be `iceServers` (camelCase). The snake_case `ice_servers` is an UNKNOWN field: serde silently drops it and the conductor runs with ZERO ICE servers — WebRTC survives on host candidates only while peers are co-located, then dies silently when topology spreads (adam→shem, 2026-05-27; 2,081 divergent anchors from the co-located era). Use `iceServers`, never `ice_servers`. The render gate `scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh` enforces this at deploy; do not ship a manifest it will reject. Evidence: Holochain conductor-config example (`iceServers`); tx5-connection `config.rs` `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/trust/.epr-meta
witness: validator `epr:validator-escalation-ladder` flagged this write. The agency charter: agents self-grant `measure`/`inject` (+ `dispatch` with a named agent and prompt) freely — observation and advisory-with-directive cannot harm. `ask`/`deny` authorship or promotion is different in kind (it narrows or blocks another agent's future writes) and requires ratified authority from the DELIBERATING COMMUNITY — today the operator+agents working this tree (the "us" of the pre-p2p era), tomorrow a qahal — never agent self-declaration: narrow-never-widen applied to governance itself. Ratification is not a solo stamp; it is PEER ACCEPTANCE AT THE BRANCH RUNG: the branch ladder is the repo's reach axis (shift/* = self; dev = community; main = commons), a governance rule on a shift branch is structurally pending, and the dev-merge acceptance IS the ratification event — the CanonizationRef of repo governance (accepting a merge includes accepting the rules we govern ourselves by). This validator fires when a `.epr-meta` write INTRODUCES an ask|deny rule (a brand-new manifest: any ask|deny rule; an existing one: compared against its prior on-disk content, so unrelated edits to an already-governed manifest never retrigger) that is not backed by a `policy: <id>@<version>` binding whose registry row's `established_by` carries deliberation provenance (`deliberated-*`, or the legacy `operator-*` rows predating this convention). An INLINE ask|deny rule with no policy binding at all is never backed: the charter requires the deliberated registry pin for that class, not a rule authored directly in the manifest. `ask` tier: routes to review (refer_reason `escalation-requires-ratification`) rather than hard-blocking, since the gate cannot itself adjudicate ratification — only an operator can. Known v1 scope gap: `when` patterns match by BASENAME only (`_matches_when` in _lib/epr_meta.py), so this binding's `.epr-meta` scope covers the legacy flat manifest form but not the directory form (`.epr-meta/manifest.md`, basename `manifest.md`) — tighten if/when that form sees adoption. Bound at the repo root (not `.claude/epr-meta/.epr-meta`): `when` patterns are basename-only and the cascade is a strict ancestor walk, so a manifest placed anywhere other than the repo root can only ever govern writes BENEATH itself — it cannot reach out to unrelated directories. A repo-wide charter needs the repo-root anchor.

subject: /projects/elohim/genesis/orchestrator/manifests/humans/_edgenode-consolidated.template.yaml
witness:
this concern already lives at scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh (the deterministic render/deploy gate that rejects the dead key by name). When an OBSERVATION says a class needs more, move the budget once (realigns the whole class) rather than editing an instance. `ask` tier: surfaces the drift + names each offending human, one keystroke (EPR_META_ACK=1) to proceed; dismissals aggregate for drift review. Static observation, no live metrics dependency — the value is reasoned once and held by the class.

witness:
this concern already lives at genesis/data/timeline/backlog/susan-kitsune2-gossip-never-attempts.md (the incident that proved the law's down-direction). LAW — archetype budget values are EVIDENCE-BOUND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Raise a value only on observed failure at the current value (OOM record, CFS-throttle evidence, crashloop trace). Lower a value only with evidence that the ORIGINAL bump's cause is cured — never on the assumption that a co-landed fix (probe, template change) was the whole cause. Record the evidence as a $-comment on the changed value IN THE SAME EDIT. Twin guard at the runtime seam: elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta (rule config-knobs-honor-the-floor).

witness:

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness: `projection_reconcile.rs` is 7344 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/rea_commitment_service.rs

(3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/replication_prioritizer.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta#guide-star (operator-set 2026-07-24; the full statement is in this manifest's body). GUIDE-STAR (operator-set 2026-07-24) — this plumbing exists so a person can EXIT their data to real community. The bar is requisite variety with the hyperscaler: k8s-grade powers (declared state, reconciliation, observability, healing) over a p2p dataplane held by communities, never landlords. The signals this code emits — peers, commitments, projection, distribution, heads, custody — are a SENSEMAKING SUBSTRATE: many folds for many witnesses (a household's reassurance, a steward's fragility view, an elohim-operator routing care at the aggregation plane). Never hardcode one privileged narrative into the substrate; make the signals true and let facings multiply. Cure toward trust: every silent bail, starved heal leg, or two-doorways-two-truths is a place a human is RIGHT not to trust yet. Convergence bar: any two doorways asked about the same commons EPR testify the SAME footprint. Destination: earned forgetting — data held so reliably that the mental load of platform surveillance dissolves, not transfers.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/tests/schema_contract.rs
witness: `schema_contract.rs` is 6188 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/conductor_admission.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 4668 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 4668 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/epr-rea/src/model.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/run-projection.py
witness:
this concern already lives at .claude/hooks/run-projection.py (the worked example — cache-keyed derivation, event-correct emission, module-level RETIRE_WHEN, measured timeout). A hook on the PROMPT path is the most expensive intervenor shape in this tree: its cost is paid on EVERY turn, so a 2s derivation is a 2s tax on every exchange for the life of the session, and a hook that blocks a turn is worse than one that says nothing. Four properties make a per-turn injector admissible, and each has already been got wrong somewhere in this tree or its siblings. (1) THE HOT PATH READS A CACHE — keyed on cheap stats, never a subprocess chain; refresh the expensive leg on SessionStart and degrade the per-turn path to an honest `refresh pending` marker rather than blocking. (2) THE EMISSION SHAPE IS EVENT-SPECIFIC — on UserPromptSubmit plain stdout reaches model context, on SessionStart/PreToolUse only the `hookSpecificOutput` JSON wrapper lands; the wrong shape ships a hook that silently never lands (recorded at pickup-semantic-surfacing.py:182-188). (3) THE TIMEOUT IS MEASURED, NOT WISHED — values are SECONDS, and this file already carries a live declared-vs-actual mismatch (load-project-context.py registers 5s while its own internal budget is 25s, unreachable by construction). Measure the cached path, then declare a number the work fits inside; if it does not fit, shrink the derivation. (4) IT DECLARES `RETIRE_WHEN` — a per-turn scaffold is exactly the class that is load-bearing on one model tier and dead weight on the next, so the exit is part of shipping it, not a footnote.
 [rule `per-turn-injector-carries-its-budget` from /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/sync-check.py
witness:
this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.
 [rule `correction-outlives-the-turn` from /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/doorway/doorway-service/src/server/http.rs
witness: `http.rs` is 7361 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: .claude/hooks/run-projection.py
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/hooks/run-projection.py (the worked example — cache-keyed derivation, event-correct emission, module-level RETIRE_WHEN, measured timeout). A hook on the PROMPT path is the most expensive intervenor shape in this tree: its cost is paid on EVERY turn, so a 2s derivation is a 2s tax on every exchange for the life of the session, and a hook that blocks a turn is worse than one that says nothing. Four properties make a per-turn injector admissible, and each has already been got wrong somewhere in this tree or its siblings. subject: .claude/hooks/run-projection.py
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/hooks/run-projection.py (the worked example — cache-keyed derivation, event-correct emission, module-level RETIRE_WHEN, measured timeout). A hook on the PROMPT path is the most expensive intervenor shape in this tree: its cost is paid on EVERY turn, so a 2s derivation is a 2s tax on every exchange for the life of the session, and a hook that blocks a turn is worse than one that says nothing. Four properties make a per-turn injector admissible, and each has already been got wrong somewhere in this tree or its siblings. (1) THE HOT PATH READS A CACHE — keyed on cheap stats, never a subprocess chain; refresh the expensive leg on SessionStart and degrade the per-turn path to an honest `refresh pending` marker rather than blocking. (2) THE EMISSION SHAPE IS EVENT-SPECIFIC — on UserPromptSubmit plain stdout reaches model context, on SessionStart/PreToolUse only the `hookSpecificOutput` JSON wrapper lands; the wrong shape ships a hook that silently never lands (recorded at pickup-semantic-surfacing.py:182-188). (3) THE TIMEOUT IS MEASURED, NOT WISHED — values are SECONDS, and this file already carries a live declared-vs-actual mismatch (load-project-context.py registers 5s while its own internal budget is 25s, unreachable by construction). Measure the cached path, then declare a number the work fits inside; if it does not fit, shrink the derivation. (4) IT DECLARES `RETIRE_WHEN` — a per-turn scaffold is exactly the class that is load-bearing on one model tier and dead weight on the next, so the exit is part of shipping it, not a footnote.

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: .claude/hooks/placement-drift-signal.py
witness: this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: genesis/orchestrator/manifests/humans/_edgenode-consolidated.template.yaml
witness: this concern already lives at scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh (the deterministic render/deploy gate that rejects the dead key by name). Evidence: Holochain conductor-config example (`iceServers`); tx5-connection `config.rs` `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.

witness:

If a build-only script (e.g. cargo-publish-*.sh) legitimately needs a richer toolchain, confirm it never runs on the deploy path before proceeding.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/api/source_chain.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
