subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/conductor_admission.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/api/attention.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

witness: validator `epr:validator-brand-vocabulary-boundary` flagged this write. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

subject: scripts/ci/run-dataplane-validation.sh
witness: this concern already lives at each deploy script's own header requirement (bash + coreutils only), scarred by edge #1183. INVARIANT — deploy-container scripts are bash + coreutils ONLY. subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/binding_mint.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-brand-vocabulary-boundary` flagged this write. Product and architecture prose may use the protocol's domain brands; compilable artifacts should name the capability an unfamiliar engineer is actually working with. Prefer identity, learning, work, community or collective governance, economy or value flow, and the precise governance concept (judgment, decision, policy, commitment, authority, or recovery quorum) in symbols, routes, schemas, persistence names, and wire values. The validator is net-new-only and ignores documentation, comments, and schema prose, so existing debt can be cleaned incrementally without tolling unrelated maintenance. This repository is still pre-compatibility: internal package ids, Holochain roles and zomes, persisted discriminators, and wire literals do not earn an exception merely because we already use them. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/binding_proof_wire.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/db/content_diesel.rs
witness: `content_diesel.rs` is 4720 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: `http.rs` is 16921 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

Product and architecture prose may use the protocol's domain brands; compilable artifacts should name the capability an unfamiliar engineer is actually working with. Prefer identity, learning, work, community or collective governance, economy or value flow, and the precise governance concept (judgment, decision, policy, commitment, authority, or recovery quorum) in symbols, routes, schemas, persistence names, and wire values. The validator is net-new-only and ignores documentation, comments, and schema prose, so existing debt can be cleaned incrementally without tolling unrelated maintenance. This repository is still pre-compatibility: internal package ids, Holochain roles and zomes, persisted discriminators, and wire literals do not earn an exception merely because we already use them. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

subject: /projects/elohim/doorway/doorway-service/src/server/http.rs
witness: `http.rs` is 8090 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/hc_client.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/api/source_chain.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/conductor_bridge_health.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-brand-vocabulary-boundary` flagged this write. Product and architecture prose may use the protocol's domain brands; compilable artifacts should name the capability an unfamiliar engineer is actually working with. Prefer identity, learning, work, community or collective governance, economy or value flow, and the precise governance concept (judgment, decision, policy, commitment, authority, or recovery quorum) in symbols, routes, schemas, persistence names, and wire values. The validator is net-new-only and ignores documentation, comments, and schema prose, so existing debt can be cleaned incrementally without tolling unrelated maintenance. This repository is still pre-compatibility: internal package ids, Holochain roles and zomes, persisted discriminators, and wire literals do not earn an exception merely because we already use them. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

subject: /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/deprecation-sentinel.py
witness:
this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.
 [rule `correction-outlives-the-turn` from /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: `mod.rs` is 9165 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: .claude/hooks/deprecation-sentinel.py
witness: this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/heartbeat.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/reanchor_backfill.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/deprecation-sentinel.py
witness:
this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.
 [rule `correction-outlives-the-turn` from /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)
 [rule `interface-first-reuse-rs` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/reanchor_backfill.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: .claude/hooks/deprecation-sentinel.py
witness: this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/api/source_chain.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/hc_client.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs

witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/signals.rs
witness: `signals.rs` is 4404 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 4995 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/behaviour.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta#guide-star (operator-set 2026-07-24; the full statement is in this manifest's body). GUIDE-STAR (operator-set 2026-07-24) — this plumbing exists so a person can EXIT their data to real community. The bar is requisite variety with the hyperscaler: k8s-grade powers (declared state, reconciliation, observability, healing) over a p2p dataplane held by communities, never landlords. The signals this code emits — peers, commitments, projection, distribution, heads, custody — are a SENSEMAKING SUBSTRATE: many folds for many witnesses (a household's reassurance, a steward's fragility view, an elohim-operator routing care at the aggregation plane). Never hardcode one privileged narrative into the substrate; make the signals true and let facings multiply. Cure toward trust: every silent bail, starved heal leg, or two-doorways-two-truths is a place a human is RIGHT not to trust yet. Convergence bar: any two doorways asked about the same commons EPR testify the SAME footprint. Destination: earned forgetting — data held so reliably that the mental load of platform surveillance dissolves, not transfers.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: genesis/a2o/scripts/__tests__/render-markdown.test.ts
witness: this concern already lives at genesis/a2o/schemas/sprint-report.schema.json (the run envelope, Ajv-strict-validated before every write in scripts/build-sprint-report.ts) + elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/views/verdict-view.schema.json (the per-check evidence). This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/metrics.rs
witness: `metrics.rs` is 5071 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: `http.rs` is 18260 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: `http.rs` is 18405 lines — at/over the 7000-line HARD LoC ceiling. A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Run `.claude/scripts/habits-project.py --check` after; the flat register at genesis/manifests/habits.yaml is a GENERATED projection of these atoms.

If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs

The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
