subject: doorway/doorway-service/src/server/http.rs
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (Step 4: Concern-Canon Answer) + doorway/doorway-service/seam-registry.yaml (this crate's decision-point registry) — where a new decision surface answers the canon and gets registered. This shape (a verdict/decision/outcome/reason enum, a `decide_*` predicate, an `Answer<T>` boundary type, or a route registration) is exactly what the seam-concern contract architecture's birth rule governs: a NEW decision predicate, boundary answer type, sync message, or route may not be born unregistered. Before shipping one: walk `p2p-design-gate` Step 4 — answer C0-C14 (`answered`/`partial`/`unbound`/`n-a`-with-justification) against the guarantee in its canon home (predicate-bearing classes are enforcement rows in `.claude/epr-meta/policies.yaml`, currently C2/C6a; the rest are Precedent-shaped rows in `.claude/epr-meta/concerns.yaml`) — then add a row to `doorway/doorway-service/seam-registry.yaml` (schema: `elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/manifest/seam-registry.schema.json`). The census (`placement-audit.py --epr-meta`) is the enforcement backstop, not this advisory: it fails loud on an unregistered point, an uncited contract test, or a mirrored test. This rule matches file CONTENT, not added lines, so an edit anywhere in an already-registered file (`http.rs`, `render/registry.rs`, `projection/epr_router.rs`, `bootstrap/k2.rs`, `cache/reach_aware_serving.rs`) re-fires too — the accepted cost of a declarative advisory that never blocks (never a validator: this is a judgement call, not a textual proof).

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5324 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p_iroh/pull_core.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-brand-vocabulary-boundary` flagged this write. Product and architecture prose may use the protocol's domain brands; compilable artifacts should name the capability an unfamiliar engineer is actually working with. Prefer identity, learning, work, community or collective governance, economy or value flow, and the precise governance concept (judgment, decision, policy, commitment, authority, or recovery quorum) in symbols, routes, schemas, persistence names, and wire values. The validator is net-new-only and ignores documentation, comments, and schema prose, so existing debt can be cleaned incrementally without tolling unrelated maintenance. This repository is still pre-compatibility: internal package ids, Holochain roles and zomes, persisted discriminators, and wire literals do not earn an exception merely because we already use them. Rename those coded references now; add a real migration boundary only after an external contract is deliberately ratified. Advisory only: teach and inventory; never block authoring.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/participations_reconcile.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta#guide-star (operator-set 2026-07-24; the full statement is in this manifest's body). GUIDE-STAR (operator-set 2026-07-24) — this plumbing exists so a person can EXIT their data to real community. The bar is requisite variety with the hyperscaler: k8s-grade powers (declared state, reconciliation, observability, healing) over a p2p dataplane held by communities, never landlords. The signals this code emits — peers, commitments, projection, distribution, heads, custody — are a SENSEMAKING SUBSTRATE: many folds for many witnesses (a household's reassurance, a steward's fragility view, an elohim-operator routing care at the aggregation plane). Never hardcode one privileged narrative into the substrate; make the signals true and let facings multiply. Cure toward trust: every silent bail, starved heal leg, or two-doorways-two-truths is a place a human is RIGHT not to trust yet. Convergence bar: any two doorways asked about the same commons EPR testify the SAME footprint. Destination: earned forgetting — data held so reliably that the mental load of platform surveillance dissolves, not transfers.

witness: this concern already lives at genesis/data/timeline/backlog/dataplane-peer-fallback-and-blob-replication.md (the peer-fallback invariant's canonical home). INVARIANT — peers are the store; doorways project with peer-fallback (race_fetch). Code writing "App not found" or "App ZIP not available" is on the EPR/blob resolution path. Root cause and fix plan (read before adding a new resolution-path NotFound arm): genesis/data/timeline/backlog/dataplane-peer-fallback-and-blob-replication.md

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5362 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: .claude/hooks/ram-guard.py
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/hooks/run-projection.py (the worked example — cache-keyed derivation, event-correct emission, module-level RETIRE_WHEN, measured timeout). A hook on the PROMPT path is the most expensive intervenor shape in this tree: its cost is paid on EVERY turn, so a 2s derivation is a 2s tax on every exchange for the life of the session, and a hook that blocks a turn is worse than one that says nothing. Four properties make a per-turn injector admissible, and each has already been got wrong somewhere in this tree or its siblings. (1) THE HOT PATH READS A CACHE — keyed on cheap stats, never a subprocess chain; refresh the expensive leg on SessionStart and degrade the per-turn path to an honest `refresh pending` marker rather than blocking. (2) THE EMISSION SHAPE IS EVENT-SPECIFIC — on UserPromptSubmit plain stdout reaches model context, on SessionStart/PreToolUse only the `hookSpecificOutput` JSON wrapper lands; the wrong shape ships a hook that silently never lands (recorded at pickup-semantic-surfacing.py:182-188). (3) THE TIMEOUT IS MEASURED, NOT WISHED — values are SECONDS, and this file already carries a live declared-vs-actual mismatch (load-project-context.py registers 5s while its own internal budget is 25s, unreachable by construction). Measure the cached path, then declare a number the work fits inside; if it does not fit, shrink the derivation. (4) IT DECLARES `RETIRE_WHEN` — a per-turn scaffold is exactly the class that is load-bearing on one model tier and dead weight on the next, so the exit is part of shipping it, not a footnote.

This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/conductor_writes.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_adoption.rs
witness: `head_adoption.rs` is 5107 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/hc_client.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/verify.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/verify.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)
 [rule `interface-first-reuse-rs` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: scripts/ci/capture-rollout-evidence.sh
witness: this concern already lives at each deploy script's own header requirement (bash + coreutils only), scarred by edge #1183. INVARIANT — deploy-container scripts are bash + coreutils ONLY. The render/deploy container has no python, no pip, no PyYAML — a script that imports one fails BEFORE `kubectl apply`, silently pinning the fleet on pre-fix builds (edge #1183 failed all 7 human deploys on a PyYAML import; it made the fixes it was gating look inert). Parse YAML/JSON with bash + coreutils (grep/sed/awk), not a python one-liner. And VERIFY where it RUNS, not just locally: a CI tool negative-tested outside its runtime is itself an unverified claim — the same class it polices. If a build-only script (e.g. cargo-publish-*.sh) legitimately needs a richer toolchain, confirm it never runs on the deploy path before proceeding.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5656 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: genesis/a2o/src/framework/devices/playwright-device.ts
witness: this concern already lives at genesis/a2o/schemas/sprint-report.schema.json (the run envelope, Ajv-strict-validated before every write in scripts/build-sprint-report.ts) + elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/views/verdict-view.schema.json (the per-check evidence). This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: genesis/a2o/src/framework/devices/playwright-device.ts
witness: this concern already lives at genesis/a2o/schemas/sprint-report.schema.json (the run envelope, Ajv-strict-validated before every write in scripts/build-sprint-report.ts) + elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/views/verdict-view.schema.json (the per-check evidence). This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: scripts/ci/stage-spa-blob.sh

Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: genesis/a2o/steps/delivery/runtime-upgrade-propagation.steps.ts
witness: this concern already lives at genesis/a2o/schemas/sprint-report.schema.json (the run envelope, Ajv-strict-validated before every write in scripts/build-sprint-report.ts) + elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/views/verdict-view.schema.json (the per-check evidence). This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: /projects/elohim/.claude/hooks/deprecation-sentinel.py
witness:
this concern already lives at .eprfs/status/flows.jsonl via `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason '...'` (the durable home for a run-scale correction). This edit reads as a CORRECTION — it reverses or supersedes an earlier decision. The reason for a reversal is the most perishable state in a run: it lands in the conversation, and compaction is lossy summarization of exactly that region, so nothing re-injects it afterward because habits and commitments were never told. Survival then depends on the summarizer's judgment, which is an outdated judgment left in charge. Worse, an operator's mid-run correction IS the algedonic channel: if the pain signal reaches only the current draft and not the state, it was absorbed by the thing that caused it. Write the correction where it outlives the window — `epr flow note --on <target> --kind correction --reason "…"` (or `--kind failed-approach --reason "tried X, it failed because Y" --switched-to "Z"`, so the next session inherits the consequence without re-attempting the dead end). The note ANNOTATES: it never discharges the commitment. This is a teaching signal, not a gate — it fires beside the per-turn projection's footer, which teaches the same write path at read time; the rule is the edit-time half of one discipline.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/elohim/zomes/content_store_integrity/build.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: genesis/a2o/steps/delivery/runtime-upgrade-propagation.steps.ts
witness: this concern already lives at genesis/a2o/schemas/sprint-report.schema.json (the run envelope, Ajv-strict-validated before every write in scripts/build-sprint-report.ts) + elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/views/verdict-view.schema.json (the per-check evidence). This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An unreachable probe is `skipped` with its reason in `summary`; a measured negative is `failed` and the decision to keep it non-blocking stays at the gate; genuinely undecidable is Decision::Refer{ContestedEvidence}. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: /projects/elohim/genesis/orchestrator/manifests/humans/_edgenode-conductor.template.yaml
witness:
this concern already lives at scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh (the deterministic render/deploy gate that rejects the dead key by name). INVARIANT — `webrtc_config` passes VERBATIM into tx5's serde-camelCase `WebRtcConfig`. The ICE-server list key MUST be `iceServers` (camelCase). The snake_case `ice_servers` is an UNKNOWN field: serde silently drops it and the conductor runs with ZERO ICE servers — WebRTC survives on host candidates only while peers are co-located, then dies silently when topology spreads (adam→shem, 2026-05-27; 2,081 divergent anchors from the co-located era). Use `iceServers`, never `ice_servers`. The render gate `scripts/ci/validate-conductor-config.sh` enforces this at deploy; do not ship a manifest it will reject. Evidence: Holochain conductor-config example (`iceServers`); tx5-connection `config.rs` `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.

subject: elohim/ark/core/src/manifest.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)
