subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/blob_store.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). (3) Cite short-form derivation (sha256:<16-hex> of the body CID) → .claude/scripts/_lib/cite_graph.py (decode-only oracle; only `eprfs cid` encodes CIDs). (4) Wire shapes / view types → elohim/sdk/schemas (generated to TS via codegen — never hand-roll a wire struct). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5702 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5799 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: .claude/hooks/ram-guard.py
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/hooks/run-projection.py (the worked example — cache-keyed derivation, event-correct emission, module-level RETIRE_WHEN, measured timeout). Four properties make a per-turn injector admissible, and each has already been got wrong somewhere in this tree or its siblings. (1) THE HOT PATH READS A CACHE — keyed on cheap stats, never a subprocess chain; refresh the expensive leg on SessionStart and degrade the per-turn path to an honest `refresh pending` marker rather than blocking. (2) THE EMISSION SHAPE IS EVENT-SPECIFIC — on UserPromptSubmit plain stdout reaches model context, on SessionStart/PreToolUse only the `hookSpecificOutput` JSON wrapper lands; the wrong shape ships a hook that silently never lands (recorded at pickup-semantic-surfacing.py:182-188). (3) THE TIMEOUT IS MEASURED, NOT WISHED — values are SECONDS, and this file already carries a live declared-vs-actual mismatch (load-project-context.py registers 5s while its own internal budget is 25s, unreachable by construction). Measure the cached path, then declare a number the work fits inside; if it does not fit, shrink the derivation. (4) IT DECLARES `RETIRE_WHEN` — a per-turn scaffold is exactly the class that is load-bearing on one model tier and dead weight on the next, so the exit is part of shipping it, not a footnote.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/dna/node-registry/zomes/node_registry_integrity/src/lib.rs
witness:
validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").
 [rule `dna-hash-neutrality` from /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/dna/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/conductor_writes.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs

A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/conductor_writes.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/p2p/projection_reconcile.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness:

Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

This file mints a result artifact, and the shape is OWNED — do not hand-roll one. A verification result is exactly three things and there is no fourth: one ASSERTION is a CheckWitness{checkId, outcome, summary, observed} (elohim/epr/src/verdict.rs); one RUN is the envelope {runId, gitCommit, env{}, declared{}} carrying checks[]; the MEMO of a run is a measure-fold@1 keyed (subject x measure@version x env). `check_id` IS the `@concern:` tag IS the `checks:` string in genesis/manifests/habits.yaml — that one identifier is the only join between this artifact, the register, and CI. Reuse it. OUTCOME IS THREE-VALUED AND CLOSED: passed | failed | skipped. There is no `warn`. An assertion that never ran is ABSENT from checks[] and surfaces in declared.notMeasured — absence is DERIVED against a denominator declared outside the run, never emitted by the runner that failed. IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. Do not conform the tool and do not write a new schema for it — declare a row in .claude/epr-meta/measures.yaml (family, procedure naming the external producer, unit naming its shape) and translate at the point of READ. Variety belongs at the edge; the core stays narrow. Reasoning: genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-verification-as-memoized-derivation-guidestar.md (§2 the classification, §5 what is refused).

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 5958 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/watch.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/apply.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/lineage_bridge.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/dna/node-registry/zomes/node_registry_integrity/src/lib.rs
witness:
validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").
 [rule `dna-hash-neutrality` from /projects/elohim/elohim/holochain/dna/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/node-registry/zomes/node_registry_integrity/src/lib.rs
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/conductor_writes.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/lineage_roles.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/readopt.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/apply.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/mod.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. (2) Canonical dag-cbor codec + compute_cid (identity-minting envelope) → elohim/epr: src/cid.rs (compute_cid), src/cbor.rs (encode/decode), src/envelope.rs (canonical_bytes). Precedent — BritCid/BlobCid divergence, 2026-07-12 consolidation spec (elohim/brit/docs/specs/2026-07-12-shared-crate-consolidation-design.md): two CID newtypes, a re-implemented drift_fingerprint, and two verdict enums drifted apart because each was re-derived instead of shared. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. (Advisory `inject` nudge — it never blocks, and it names no validator: "is this a re-implementation?" is a judgement, not a textual predicate.)

IF THE BYTES COME FROM A TOOL WE DO NOT OWN (cucumber-js, cargo test, clippy, junit): that is a FOREIGN measure. subject: .claude/data/lineage-carry-metrics.jsonl
witness: this concern already lives at .claude/scripts/_lib/findings_ledger.py (the shared row primitive and the live-set vs append-only mode contract). A new ledger here IS a legitimate birth — this directory's own guide says so — and that is exactly where the cost is decided, so decide it before the first row. (1) REACH the row primitive: _lib/findings_ledger.py already owns the shape ({fp, first_seen, status, ...}), the flock'd read-check-append, and the drain. A second hand-rolled appender is a second ontology. (2) DECLARE THE MODE, because the two are not interchangeable: LIVE-SET (one row per live condition, DELETED when it drains — reading answers "what is wrong now") or APPEND-ONLY (every row a historical fact, never removed — reading answers "what happened"). An append-only ledger that gets drained destroys the growth-rate measure it exists to compute. (3) NAME THE READER, by path, in this manifest. governance-findings.jsonl reached 7,806,004 bytes with zero readers — a repo-wide grep for read/load/open against its name returns nothing — and genesis/manifests/habits.yaml has said so since it was 4.3MB. Two more ledgers here are 0 bytes. A writer without a reader is the instrument-with-no-reader shape this layer has grown at least six times. (4) DECLARE A FORGETTING RULE (a count, an age, or a comet tier), and if any row can be standing evidence for an open question, a PIN that survives it — SET AND RELEASED BY A DECISION, NEVER BY A CLOCK. Rotation without a pin deletes the evidence for an unresolved question on a counter; a pin without a release is a leak wearing a policy's clothes. The shape already exists four times in this repo and is nowhere named: Jenkins buildDiscarder(logRotator(numToKeepStr)) runs at 20/100/50/30/30 with no keepLog pin anywhere; memkit-retention.py's HEAD/TAIL/CORE comet keeps a permanent spine but releases it automatically; .epr-meta `retire-when:` is a decision-gated pin for RULES; habits.yaml `best_observed:` is one for a high-water mark. Nothing pins a result or a ledger row.

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/release_adoption/carry.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?
 [rule `conductor-call-is-uncancellable` from /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/.epr-meta]

subject: /projects/elohim/elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/lineage_bridge.rs
witness:
this concern already lives at genesis/data/timeline/backlog/arch-scale-risk-backlog.md. SCALE RISK ON THIS PATH — row 3 of the scale-risk cluster: the sweep has EVERY crossed peer held-carry EVERY neighbour's v1 records (DHT writes ∝ peers × records), one 16-record page per 30 s tick, so a 3.5k-record neighbour is ≈110 min per courier and the window stays open at least that long. Three peers on node_registry hides it. Prefer changes that elect a courier or compact what is carried over changes that only tune the page size, and put the catch-up minutes on the receipt. Advisory only.

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/lineage_roles.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/lineage_roles.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/elohim-storage/src/services/head_batch_resolver.rs (module doc: the fallback rule + the in-wasm BATCH_EXTERN_BUDGET discipline) + .claude/skills/p2p-design-gate/SKILL.md (the conductor call you cannot cancel). `HcClient::call_zome` has no timeout and no cancellation path (`hc_client.rs:405`) — a caller-side timeout abandons the call while the conductor keeps executing it with nobody listening, still holding the read permit whose saturation the timeout was reacting to. The T13 spike (2026-08-08-conductor-call-deadline-capability-spike.md) qualifies this: the client API already declares a timeout (`CallZomeOptions::timeout`) but enforces it CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, and most slow-call cost is DB-permit queue-wait that IS cancellable-on-drop (a tokio semaphore permit returns) — only the wasm BODY is non-interruptible once started. Design every conductor-touching surface so the WORK is bounded BEFORE the call is made: batch externs (`content_store::resolve_content_heads_local` / `resolve_canonical_elections`) carry their OWN in-wasm deadline (`BATCH_BUDGET_DEFAULT_MS`/`BATCH_BUDGET_CEILING_MS`) and return partial results (`unattempted`, never a failure); callers size batches (`services::head_batch_resolver::HeadBatchResolver`) and interpret `unattempted`/ `stop_reason`, never bolt a caller-side timeout onto `call_zome` and call it bounded. If you are adding a new `call_zome`/`CallZomeOptions` call site, ask: is the WORK bounded on the WASM side before this call is made, or does a caller timeout merely abandon a conductor that keeps running?

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs

subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/http.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs (BlobCid) + elohim/epr/src/{cid,cbor,envelope}.rs (the canonical codec) — the interfaces this write may be re-deriving. REUSE the canonical interface before authoring a bespoke CID / fingerprint / dag-cbor / verdict implementation — do not re-derive identity math or the codec. Canonical homes: (1) Addressing (CID compute / compute_raw / short_fingerprint) → eprfs-core::BlobCid, elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/address.rs. Prefer a shared crate over a parallel reimplementation. subject: elohim/elohim-storage/src/main.rs
witness: `main.rs` is 6101 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/node-registry/zomes/node_registry_coordinator/src/lib.rs
witness: `lib.rs` is 4027 lines — over the 3000-line soft LoC ceiling (hard ceiling: 7000). A first-party source file past the hard ceiling is a god-file: it corrodes its own governance (line-number invariant anchors drift every edit; two-location sync traps grow ~1000 lines apart) and outgrows what one context window can review. Soft ceiling = edit-time nudge (new logic likely belongs in a module). Hard ceiling = a fingerprinted architecture finding: canonicalize a modularization plan into the timeline backlog and drive it as bounded work — never refactor mid-edit. Refactor-safety asymmetry the reviewer must honor: coordinator zomes hot-swap via update_coordinators (cheap); integrity-zome changes move the DNA hash (reinstall/partition trap — ride a deliberate DNA-lineage event only); plain native Rust is gated by fmt/clippy/nextest alone. Ratchet ceilings DOWN as the tail drains; never up.

subject: elohim/holochain/dna/node-registry/zomes/node_registry_integrity/Cargo.toml
witness: validator `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` flagged this write. HASH-MOVING vs COORDINATOR-ONLY — classify before you plan the landing. The Holochain DNA hash is computed over the INTEGRITY zomes plus the modifiers; coordinator zomes are outside it (`uhCok…` in an error is a WASM hash, `uhC0k…` a DNA hash). Consequences, not style points: a coordinator-only diff heals via the conductor's `update_coordinators` hot-swap — no re-key, no DHT churn, gated by ALLOW_COORDINATOR_UPDATE. An integrity-zome or modifiers diff cannot: it needs a reinstall (ALLOW_DNA_REINSTALL, non-prod true by default), the reinstall mints a NEW agent key, and force-reinstalling SOME peers in a namespace but not all lands them on different DNA hashes — different DHTs — a P2P partition (the alpha genesis PAIR must both get the flag). The validator LABELS the hash-moving class and stays silent on the coordinator-only one: the cheap path carries no trap, and an advisory on every coordinator edit would be the nag this registry exists to avoid. It never blocks. If the change can be expressed coordinator-side, do that; if it genuinely belongs in integrity, ride a planned lineage event with the whole namespace. Registry note: this rule is INLINE by design — `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is registered machinery with NO concern-canon row, because the ceremony tested DNA-hash-neutrality as a class and declined it ("no runtime predicate… it becomes the third registered validator, not a class").

subject: elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/src/tests/lamad.rs
witness: this concern already lives at elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest/tests/lamad.rs `unique_id()` (the helper that IS the cure; dna #1357). INVARIANT — sweettest retries share the process-global kitsune2 mem-bootstrap store. A `create_content` (or `test_content(...)`) call with a FIXED string id (e.g. "test-1", "tier-x") makes a nextest RETRY re-join the first attempt's DHT residue, so `create_content` refuses with "already exists" and the retry can never pass — the fixed id self-poisons the retry (dna #1357). Use `unique_id("base")` (the epoch-nanos-suffixed helper in `tests/lamad.rs`) for any id that a multi-conductor or gossip-visible scenario writes, so every attempt gets fresh ids while the scenario stays byte-identical.
